answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to post a bond in a shared vault and earn access through randomly assigned trades with established peers. Peers issue signed, time-limited attestations only after observing useful work, while a challenge agent can expose collusion; proven fraud burns the bond and taints linked reputations. Creating many identities therefore demands repeated capital lockups and genuine labor, so an attacker cannot cheaply flood the ocean or hide behind a knoll.
